items.title: fix(data): make val max_samples subsample follow validation_shuffle
items.bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #7824

## What

`val_max_samples` subsampling ran under `data.shuffle` because `RLHFDataset` reads a single `shuffle` flag from the config that both the train and val datasets share. With the default `legacy_data.yaml` (`shuffle: True`, `validation_shuffle: False`), the val subsample was random, contradicting `validation_shuffle` and breaking validation reproducibility across restarts.

`create_rl_dataset` now maps `data.validation_shuffle` onto the dataset-level `shuffle` flag when `is_train=False`, so the val subsample follows the same flag the val dataloader sampler already uses (`trainer_base.py` / `ray_trainer.py`), and `validation_shuffle=False` yields a deterministic head slice. When `validation_shuffle` is unset, behavior is unchanged (falls back to `data.shuffle`).

## How to check

New CPU test file `tests/utils/dataset/test_rl_dataset_validation_shuffle_on_cpu.py` (5 cases: val follows validation_shuffle; train still follows shuffle; fallback when unset; seeded random subsample is reproducible; caller config not mutated).

```
pytest tests/utils/dataset/test_rl_dataset_validation_shuffle_on_cpu.py -v  # 5 passed
ruff check && ruff format --check  # clean
```

Verified the core case fails on `main` (subsample is random: `selected 8 random samples out of 64`) and passes with this change (deterministic head slice rows 0-7).

## AI use disclosure (per AGENTS.md)

- The fix and tests were prepared with AI assistance (ZCode, GLM). I have reviewed the full diff line by line and can defend every change.
- Duplicate check done on 2026-10-08: no open PR touches `validation_shuffle` or the `create_rl_dataset` val path. The nearest PR is #7819 (same reporter, fixes the sister issue #7816 by seeding the train `max_samples` rng) — it does not wire `validation_shuffle` into the val subsample; this change is complementary, not overlapping.

items.title: LMCache + vLLM: pipeline parallelism now works with MLA models (Kimi K2, GLM-4.6)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## LMCache + vLLM: pipeline parallelism now works with MLA models (Kimi K2, GLM-4.6)

Just wanted to give a heads-up here because I've seen a few issues pop up about LMCache + PP not working, and I've put up a fix on the LMCache side that unblocks it.

### What was broken

If you tried to run vLLM with LMCache in multi-server MP mode with `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1`, the connector would refuse to start with:

```
ValueError: LMCacheMPConnector multi-server mode only supports
tensor parallelism (TP), not pipeline parallelism (PP). Got pp_size=2.
```

This hit especially hard for MLA models (Kimi K2, GLM-4.5/4.6) because those are exactly the workloads where you want both PP (to fit a large model across nodes) and LMCache (to cut TTFT on long-context agentic workloads).

### Why it was blocked

The guard existed because of a subtle read-lock refcounting bug. `compute_extra_count` in LMCache inferred whether a model used MLA by checking `tp > world_size`. That heuristic is correct when PP=1 but breaks under PP>1 — PP inflates `world_size` to `tp × pp`, so the inference produces `extra_count = 0` when it should be `tp_size - 1`. Result: the server under-locks, multiple workers race on the same KV chunk, and you get premature eviction.

### The fix

I opened [LMCache PR #4082](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4082) that:

1. Carries an explicit `use_mla` flag in the cache key (instead of inferring it) — backward-compatible on the wire
2. Fixes `kv_tp_size` and `is_kv_writer` in `ParallelStrategy` to account for the fact that server blocks align with PP stages, not TP groups
3. Propagates `use_mla` across all client adapters (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, SDK)

No vLLM-side changes are needed — vLLM's in-tree connector already imports from the `lmcache` package, so once the LMCache fix lands and users update, it picks up the fix automatically. items.title: [Bug]: NIXL P/D disagg silently corrupts output when hybrid-attention layers share a storage base with different block lengths (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash served via NIXL PD disaggregation (2P×TP8 + 2D×TP8, 2×H200 nodes, RDMA) produces garbled output (nonsensical characters, or empty content/reasoning fields) with no errors or crashes — silent data corruption. The same image serves a single-full-attention model (GLM-5.3) correctly in the same topology. Mooncake, CUDA graphs, and MultiConnector were ruled out.

### Root cause

In `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py`, region registration deduplicates transfer regions by `base_addr` alone, and the collapsed branch only refreshes `block_len/stride/num_blocks` when `is_mla_region` is true.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's `layers.2.attn.compressor.state_cache` (`CircularBufferSpec`, needs block_len=32768) shares its storage base address with `layers.0.attn.swa_cache` (MLA, block_len=19008). It folds into region 0 without updating block_len, so its compressor state is transferred with only 19008 bytes per block and offsets computed from the swa view — truncated and misaligned. `layers.2.attn.indexer.k_cache` hits a second instance of the same base-address conflict.

Diagnostic signature: the affected region simultaneously shows `rgid=-1` (shared), `scratch=True`, and `is_mla=True` — three mutually contradictory attributes. After the fix, `num_regions` grows 12 → 14.

### Fix

Deduplicate by `(base_addr, block_len)`: regions with distinct transfer geometry stay separate; identical-geometry aliases still fold as before. A PR follows.

### Verification

- Cluster (2×8 H200, P/D disagg): before the fix — all-garbled short completions, 200-token generations fully corrupted, Chinese chat returns empty content/reasoning; after the fix — normal English/Chinese output, 0% garble rate over 200-token generations, clean output across 6 concurrent streams.
- Unit tests: new regression test fails on HEAD and passes with the fix; the existing NIXL unit test failure set is byte-identical before/after (no regressions).

items.title: [Question][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer: does the 640-token block table reach 32-pool pages on gfx942/gfx950 too?
items.bodyExcerpt:
We found this on hardware vLLM doesn't support (gfx1030, Radeon Pro V620), running GLM-5.3-Flash without aiter. The code path involved is shared with gfx942/gfx950, and we have no MI300/MI355 to check it on. Could someone with one confirm or rule it out?

**What we see.** `Glm5NextIndexerCache` stores pooled keys in pages of 32 pools (storage block 128 tokens at `index_kpool=4`). The hybrid KDA page rule makes the attention block 640. On ROCm the sparse-MLA and indexer backends accept `MultipleOf(16)` (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`), so `select_common_block_size` keeps kernel block 640. The indexer metadata builder only converts the table when the storage block is a multiple of the kernel block (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`, prefill and decode branches; unchanged on main):

```python
if (
    kernel_block_size is not None
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size != kernel_block_size
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size % kernel_block_size == 0
):
    factor = self.kv_cache_spec.block_size // kernel_block_size
    indexer_block_table = (block_table[:, ::factor] // factor).contiguous()
```

128 % 640 ≠ 0, so the 640-token table goes to `get_compressed_slot_mapping` (the kpool writer) and to `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` as if each entry named one 32-pool page. With per-chunk block allocation:
- pools written before their block exists land in padding;
- positions past the allocated blocks alias block 0;
- positions past the 52-column table (at `max_model_len` 32768) are masked by the gather.

On NVIDIA the kernel block is 64, so the `// factor` branch applies. As far as we can tell nothing here is aiter-specific: the kpool path uses `forward_cuda` on ROCm whether aiter is on or off.

**Reproducer.** One GPU, stock vLLM only, no model: [`repro_rocm_kpool_table.py`](https://github.com/Omnicef/vllm/blob/glm53-v030/tests/local/repro_rocm_kpool_table.py). It writes a 9,432-token prompt in the served prefill chunks with the real ROCm kpool writer

items.title: [Bug]: HiSparse prefill can OOM a running server (unreserved host-history staging)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

vLLM main @ ad0f67a7ec, 1×B200, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV, Model Runner V2.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With HiSparse, a prompt that the server accepted can crash EngineCore with CUDA OOM, and running requests die with it. Two allocations in the HiSparse sparse-MLA prefill path aren't reserved by startup memory profiling. The profiling dummy run is one chunk of short pure prefills.

- **Full-history copy.** `stage_prefill_rows` → `HiSparseRuntime.gather_prefill_cache` copies the prefilling request's entire history from host into a temporary GPU buffer, one layer at a time: `(cdiv(seq_len, block_size), block_size, row_bytes)`, about 0.55 GiB at 1M tokens with 576 B rows. It is freed before the next layer, so it never holds the whole KV, but it grows with prompt length and nothing reserves it.
- **Decode/prefill output join.** In mixed batches, decode and prefill run as two kernels joined by `torch.cat`, about 1 GiB at 16K batched tokens.

There are two scenarios:

1. **Prompt fits on GPU, batched with decodes** (common aggregated serving). The copy and the join are both unnecessary here, because every page is GPU-resident. They run only because of the `num_decode_tokens == 0 and all_context_pages_resident` condition in `flashinfer_mla_sparse.py`. FlashAttn and FlashInfer SM120 have the same condition, and FlashMLA sparse BF16 copies on every prefill. Fixed by #60417.
2. **Prompt spilled to host**, e.g. a 1M-token prompt reaching a HiSparse decoder whose GPU can't hold its KV. The copy is required here, and its buffer is still not reserved. Fixed by #60424, which reserves a staging buffer at startup, sized for `max_model_len`.

The model is cut to 4 layers, so a 1M-token prompt fits on one B200's GPU and this exercises scenario 1, not 2.

  hits use sliding-window rules, and NIXL transfers only its tail (`blocks_per_sw = cdiv(2048, 64) + 1`).

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Your current environment
- GLM-5.3 (78 MLA + 21 indexer layers) with a DFlash2 draft (6 layers, GQA, 8 KV heads, fp8 KV, k=4).
- Prefill DEP8 (TP1 per rank). Decode TP4. Pull-mode `NixlConnector`, GPU-resident KV (no host buffer).
- vLLM main @ `4e0a414c44`, plus #58471 (GQA draft head slicing under an MLA target), the NVFP4
  prefill-context gather from #58744, and our NVFP4 KV decode path (`nvfp4_ds_mla` on
  `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, #59342).
- GB200 NVL72 (NIXL over NVLink), and B300 HGX (NIXL over RDMA).

## Describe the issue

### 1. Whole-row transfer is unreachable for page-contiguous BLHNC MLA caches
#53781 (HiSparse host-resident hot-buffering) put `not page_contiguous` in front of the
"packed MLA layouts transfer the complete storage row" branch of
`NixlConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches`:

```python
# before #53781
elif storage_is_block_major and (
    (packed_storage and is_mla_region)
    or (not hnc_contiguous and not self._is_csa_linear)
):
# after #53781
elif storage_is_block_major and (
    not page_contiguous
    and ((packed_storage and is_mla_region) or not self._is_csa_linear)
):
```

The gate is needed so a HiSparse decoder can land host-resident and device-only layers separately.
But `page_contiguous` is true for every GLM-5.3 layer, so a device-resident BLHNC cache registers one
region per layer. Every transfer then carries one descriptor per layer per block, and BLHNC
ends up costing more than LBHNC, the opposite of its purpose.

items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

I want to start a discussion on how implicit reasoning end can break structured ouptuts + spec decode.

### Background

For structured outputs, we only apply constrained decoding after reasoning ends. This is to allow models to reason while constraining the user-visible content.

At each decode step, the scheduler roughly calls:
1. `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` to validate the draft tokens need constraining and trim any grammar-invalid tokens
2. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` to create bitmasks for the draft tokens that need constraining
3. `StructuredOutputManager.accpet_tokens` to advance grammar FSM over the constrained tokens

These three methods rely on a `StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_start` helper to identify when reasoning ends. It returns `reasoning_end_index + 1`

### Implicit Reasoning Ends

Reasoning end is usually marked by a special token (e.g. `</think>` for GLM 5.3). However, reasoning can also end implicitly when the model starts emitting content or tool call without closing reasoning first (e.g. `<think> ... <tool_call>` instead of `<think> ... </think><tool_call>`). This presents challenges for strcutured output constraint start detection.

### Issues with Implicit Reasoning Ends

Currently, `StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_start` assumes all reasoning end markers are explicit. For example, given `prefix <tool_call> suffix`,
1. `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` doesn't validate the `<tool_call>`
2. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` to create bitmasks for `suffix` only
3. `StructuredOutputManager.accpet_tokens` to advance grammar FSM over accepted `suffix` + bonux token only.

- I1: `<tool_call>` may not be grammar valid, yet it is unconditionally accepted
- I2: if a model is required to make a tool call, it will be forced to generate duplicate `<tool_call>` because the grammar isn't aware of the first one #59608

# Issue #49141 — Fused_moe dimension mismatch for Qwen MXFP4 model on ROCm

## 1. Root cause

The issue has two reports. Both are the same underlying defect: **a MoE layer whose
expert weights are stored *unquantized* in the checkpoint is still given a
*quantized* MoE method**, so the allocated parameters do not match the checkpoint
tensors.

The trigger in both cases is the MTP (speculative-decoding drafter) layer. AMD's
Quark and community GPTQ quantizations of `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` quantize the 40
transformer layers but leave the MTP layer's experts in bf16. The main model
loads fine; only the drafter fails.

* **Original MXFP4/Quark report** (`RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (256) must
  match the size of tensor b (512) at non-singleton dimension 1`, in
  `routed_experts.py::_load_w2`).
  `hidden_size=2048`, `moe_intermediate_size=512`. Quark MXFP4 allocates
  `w2_weight` as `(E, hidden, intermediate // 2)` = `(E, 2048, 256)` (fp4 packs
  two values per byte), while the checkpoint's MTP `down_proj.weight` is the
  unquantized `(2048, 512)`. `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`'s
  `quantization_config.exclude` lists `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.<i>.{gate,up,down}_proj`
  for all 256 experts, but `should_ignore_layer()` only compared the *parent*
  layer name `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts` against those *child* entries.
  **This half is already fixed on main** by the `check_children` argument added
  to `quark/utils.py::should_ignore_layer` (the amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 fix), which is
  why a commenter on the issue could not reproduce it on main. No change needed.

  `AttributeError: 'RoutedExperts' object has no attribute 'w2_weight'. Did you
  mean: 'w2_qweight'?`, same drafter-loading path).

items.title: [Kernel][Core][Shared-PCP][Capacity] Owner-shard KV history for up to 4x capacity
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Prefill context parallelism (PCP) requires every rank to attend over the complete historical Main KV and Indexer K state. Keeping that persistent history replicated on every PCP rank limits usable context length.

This change adds an opt-in owner-sharded history path for GLM-5.2 sparse attention. Each historical cache page has one physical owner, while CUDA VMM exposes a stable rank-major peer view to every PCP rank. The result is up to **4x persistent KV capacity on PCP4**, without a per-layer historical-KV collective or a persistent history replica. Pure prefill uses a bounded transient local working set.

Set `VLLM_USE_PCP_OWNER_HISTORY=1` to enable the feature. Feature-off execution preserves the standard PCP path.

## Shared-PCP positioning

This is one self-contained **Shared-PCP** optimization. Shared-PCP names a single-node PCP data model in which cross-rank tensors are exposed as explicitly placed shared GPU objects. An object may be replicated by direct peer stores, owner-sharded and peer-read, or compactly published to its consumers. The name describes data semantics rather than cache coherence or a required transport.

This PR applies that model to **owner-sharded persistent history**: each Main KV and Indexer K page has one physical owner, while stable peer mappings expose the complete logical history to every PCP rank. Peer virtual mappings do not create persistent replicas, and the bounded pure-prefill materialization workspace is transient.

## Design

For logical page `p`:

```text
owner_rank = p % pcp_size
local_page = p // pcp_size
```

- Allocate one owner-local Main KV and Indexer K shard per rank.
- Exchange CUDA allocation handles during initialization and map all shards into stable rank-major peer views.
- Fuse owner selection, FP8 quantization, local-slot translation, and persistent cache stores so each new row is written once to its owner.
- Publish completed stores with a system-scope release/acquire fence. The fence orders mem

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip redundant sparse index remap on non-indexer layers
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

With cross-layer index sharing, only some attention layers update the shared top-k buffer.
The old path still remapped that buffer on every layer.

This PR runs the remap only when the layer owns an indexer. For GLM-5.2 with
`index_topk_freq = 4`, this reduces remaps from 78 to 21 per forward pass.

## Safety

- Layer 0 always owns an indexer, so the shared output is initialized before reuse.
- Non-indexer layers do not change the inputs to the remap.
- The default `index_topk_freq = 1` path is unchanged.
- Speculative decoding still remaps on every layer.

## Update: indexer and non-indexer layers are two KV cache groups

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53781  added the is_index_group_leader field to MLAAttentionSpec: `is_index_group_leader=self.indexer is not None,`. Layers can only share a KV cache group if they agree on is_index_group_leader, so once the flag is set per layer, indexer and non-indexer layers land in different groups and therefore get different metadata instances with separate paged_kv_indices

```
index_group_leader_set = {spec.is_index_group_leader for spec in specs}
assert (
    ...
    and len(index_group_leader_set) == 1
    ...
), (
    "All attention layers in the same KV cache group must use the same "
    "... index-sharing role, ..."
)

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

With `data_parallel_size > 1` and expert parallel enabled, only some DP ranks may hold tokens on a given engine step while others schedule zero tokens. Idle ranks must still run a dummy forward so per-layer EP collectives stay in lockstep; otherwise the busy rank deadlocks in all2all.

Today `execute_model` only runs that dummy when `distributed_executor_backend == "external_launcher"`. Multiproc / MoRIIO WideEP disagg uses a different backend, so zero-token ranks skip the dummy and hang.

Headless / idle ranks may only enter via `Worker.execute_dummy_batch`. That path must also always `_dummy_run(1)` for `dp_size > 1`. Do **not** skip via a sticky latch set by `execute_model`: under dp_lockstep the latch can remain `True` across later engine steps when `execute_dummy_batch` was not paired with the call that set it. Skipping a needed dummy desyncs EP ranks (GLM-5.2 tip WideEP mid-gsm8k hang). Same-step double dummy is safe; a skipped dummy is not.

## Changes

* `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` (`execute_model`):
  * On zero-token steps, run `_dummy_run(1)` whenever `data_parallel_size > 1` (not only `external_launcher`).
* `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py` (`execute_dummy_batch`):
  * When `data_parallel_size > 1`, always `_dummy_run(1)` (no sticky early-return).

Fuse the clamped MoE activation path into FP8 block-128 activation quantization:

1. finite SwiGLU clamping;
2. BF16 SiLU and gated multiplication;
3. dynamic E4M3 block quantization, including Hopper DeepGEMM UE8M0 scales; and
4. optional filtering of invalid or non-local expert rows.

items.title: [KVConnector][NIXL] Opt-in per-layer overlapped WRITE-push for disaggregated KV transfer
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary / motivation

The stock `NixlConnector` transfers KV as a single, monolithic READ at the end of
prefill, so KV transfer does **not** overlap with prefill compute. On
disaggregated (P/D-split) inference this leaves throughput on the table versus
push-style transports.

This PR adds an **opt-in, per-layer overlapped WRITE-push** path: the prefill
side pushes each layer's KV to the decode worker as soon as that layer is
computed, overlapping KV transfer with the tail of prefill and closing the
throughput gap against push-style connectors — while staying on the open,
standard UCX/NIXL path.

Design notes / rationale live in the commit message and inline docstrings in
`push_worker.py` (module docstring describes the event-driven push pipeline).

## Design

- **Per-layer save hook** (`save_kv_layer`): records a CUDA event per layer and
  enqueues **one RDMA WRITE per KV region off-thread**, so the forward thread is
  never blocked on transfer.
- **Seal** (`wait_for_save`): finalizes the request. A model-agnostic
  **"completeness sweep"** at seal time writes any KV regions **not** covered by
  a per-layer hook (e.g. the GLM-5.1 DSA indexer caches), guaranteeing no stale
  KV is left on the decode side.
- **Scheduler bookkeeping** (`push_scheduler.py`): producer/consumer tracking
  suppresses the monolithic WRITE when layer-wise mode is on, and holds the
  engine loop open until the per-layer WRITEs complete.
- **D-side robustness fixes** (small, independently useful):
  - Seed `remote_*` params on the abort/reject recv path so an aborted/rejected
    request no longer `KeyError`s the EngineCore.
  - Handle `num_external_tokens <= 0` (full prefix-cache hit / no external
    tokens) by flipping `do_remote_prefill` off instead of staging an unseeded
    recv.

## Opt-in & safety

- Gated entirely by env var **`VLLM_NIXL_LAYERWISE_PUSH`** (plus
  **`VLLM_NIXL_LAYERWISE_DEFER_TIMEOUT`** for the deferred-write watchdog).

## Summary

- route rope-free sparse MLA to the ROCm Triton implementation for every KV-cache dtype
- dequantize FP8 KV rows in the Triton ragged-prefill kernel using the layer KV scale while keeping Q in model dtype
- use 64-bit query-row offsets so wide, long-context prefills cannot overflow 32-bit pointer arithmetic
- preserve custom MLA geometry and FP8 cache dtype in the attention benchmark harness

## Problem

AITER precompiled sparse MLA kernels assume the DeepSeek cache-row geometry: 512 latent elements plus 64 RoPE elements. GLM-5.3-Flash is rope-free and stores a 512-element row. The existing Triton ragged path already handles the NoPE geometry. This change makes its routing geometry-based instead of BF16-only, adds scaled FP8 KV dequantization, and avoids FP8-quantizing Q for that path.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`disable_any_whitespace` does not disable whitespace on the xgrammar backend — it **makes whitespace mandatory**, and as a side effect masks out the token the model wants at every JSON value position.

xgrammar's `any_whitespace=False` selects a *fixed* JSON format rather than a whitespace-free one. Its docstring is explicit that the format follows `json.dumps()` conventions, and with `separators` left unset the default is `(", ", ": ")` — *with* spaces. `backend_xgrammar.py` never passes `separators`, so today the flag requires a space after every comma and colon.

The second-order effect is the damaging one. Because the space is mandatory, the bare `"` that opens a string value becomes illegal at the value position. Measured on the mask with a real GLM-5.3 tokenizer, immediately after `{"location":`:

| grammar config | allowed tokens | whitespace-leading | bare `"` | digit-leading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `any_whitespace=True` | 1450 | 719 | yes | 395 |
| `any_whitespace=False`, default separators — **today** | 268 | **268, all of them** | **banned** | 0 |
| `any_whitespace=False`, `separators=(",", ":")` — **this PR** | 703 | **0** | yes | 395 |

The middle row is what vLLM produces now: every legal continuation begins with a space. A model prompted for minified JSON wants the bare `"`; with it masked out, probability mass shifts to the whitespace-prefixed set, where `␣0`, `␣1`, `␣-` compete with `␣"`.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55569. Related: #56457 reports the same allocation pattern in the Qwen4Exp QSA indexer, with fixes proposed for that path in #56500 and #57105 (both open); #55572 (closed) lowered the default logits budget on integrated GPUs instead.

The dense sparse-MLA indexer (`sparse_attn_indexer.py`, and the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool variant under `models/glm5next`) scores each prefill chunk with DeepGEMM's `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`, which allocates its `[M, N]` fp32 logits inside the C++ API. `N` is the request's compressed context so far, so every chunk of a long prefill asks for a tensor of a new, larger size: one launch per chunk of growing size while `M * N * 4` fits the `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` budget (512 MiB), and, once a chunk exceeds it (about 116k tokens at a 4,608-token chunk with kpool 4), several launches per chunk that are all close to the budget but never the same size twice. PyTorch's caching allocator serves a request from a cached block only if it fits, and returns segments to the driver only on `empty_cache` or an OOM-time release, so once the free space that happens to be around is used up, each chunk step adds a new segment for the rest of the prefill. On a discrete GPU this is reserved-but-idle memory; on unified-memory devices (DGX Spark / GB10) it comes out of the host's share, and the driver-level failure (`NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY`) arrives before the allocator's OOM retry can help, ending in the swap storms reported in #55569.

**Change.** Allocate the logits at a fixed width instead of the chunk's kv length, using the `max_seqlen_k` argument DeepGEMM already provides: the kernel still computes only `[cu_seqlen_ks, cu_seqlen_ke)` per row, `max_seqlen_k` is only the allocation stride, and DeepGEMM asserts `clean_logits=False` with it (verified at vLLM's pinned commit). items.bodyExcerpt:
## Error

MTP with native DSA-indexer decode above `next_n=2` crashes during warm-up on MI355X (seen at `next_n=3` and `next_n=6`). GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, `num_speculative_tokens=5` (`next_n=6`), Gluon paged MQA logits:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x20465ea0) on address 0x792dc0bf1000. Reason: Unknown.
```

Where it does not crash, the indexer silently uses wrong causal bounds: in a direct call at `next_n=3`, the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row (9/12 rows correct).

## Cause

With native decode (`next_n > 1`), `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` receives a `(B, next_n)` table of per-row context lengths, `[b, j] = L_b - next_n + j + 1`, built in [`indexer.py#L1136-L1152`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2df122e65e87dc12870ce5f0180b49f012e7a53b/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py#L1136-L1152). The AITER Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernels read the table as a flat `[B]` array and some sequences get another row's length.

Example: 4 requests, `next_n=3`, context lengths 8192 / 1500 / 3000 / 700:

| `b` | `j=0` | `j=1` | `j=2` | `L_b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8190 | 8191 | **8192** | 8192 |
| 1 | 1498 | 1499 | **1500** | 1500 |
| 2 | 2998 | 2999 | **3000** | 3000 |
| 3 | 698 | 699 | **700** | 700 |

The kernel expects `[8192, 1500, 3000, 700]` and computes each row's bound itself. Reading the `(4, 3)` table as `[4]`, it gets the first four values in memory, `[8190, 8191, 8192, 1498]`: request 0 loses its last 2 positions in every row, and requests 1 to 3 get lengths past their own KV pages, the likely source of the fault. Column `j = next_n - 1` equals `L_b`, which is what the kernel needs.

## Fix

Pass the kernels the last column, which is the per-sequence length. `[B]` and `(B, 1)` inputs, the C4A Triton path and the torch fallback are unchanged.

## Purpose

Block id 0 is the null block. It is shared by every KV cache group and is assumed to stay zero. Since #35431, the runners mark rows that own no state with 0 in the block table, not `PAD_SLOT_ID`: dummy runs, CUDA graph capture and padding rows all carry 0. items.title: [KV Offload] Split the CPU offload region across shm files
items.bodyExcerpt:
Pre-faulting the CPU offload region is capped by its single `/dev/shm` file: page-cache inserts into one shmem file are serialized, so more workers or threads stop helping. On one H200 node, eight processes pre-faulting disjoint parts of a 64 GiB file reach 9.8 GiB/s in total. Given one file each, they reach 24.6 GiB/s, and sixteen files reach 44.8 GiB/s. #59430 hits the same ceiling with threads.

Split the region's rows over up to 32 files of at least 1 GiB each. The files are mapped back to back over one anonymous reservation, so the region stays contiguous. Workers with per-rank slots start pre-faulting on different files. Regions under 2 GiB, and other users of `SharedOffloadRegion`, keep a single file.

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main):

items.title: [KV Offload] Give each rank its own CPU region outside the replicated layout
items.bodyExcerpt:
Outside the replicated layout, ranks never read each other's slots, but they still share one region whose rows interleave all ranks. Every rank pre-faults and pins its strided slots in the same shm file, contending with the others.

Give each rank its own region holding only its slots, in its own shm file. No other process maps that file, so the rank no longer waits on the cross-worker barrier before unlinking it. The replicated layout keeps the shared region.

## Overview

Adds an `mxfp4_mla` KV cache dtype for the ROCm AITER sparse MLA backend on rope-free (NoPE) latents such as GLM-5.3-Flash. Each 512-wide latent is stored as 256 bytes of E2M1 codes plus 16 inline E8M0 scales (one per 32 values): 272 bytes per token against 1024 for bf16, or 3.76× more tokens per GiB of KV cache.

This is the first of the smaller PRs split out of #59739, as requested there. It contains only the cache format, the write path and a Triton read path. Everything is Triton or Python: no HIP or C++ sources, and no new environment variables.

## Claims

- **KV capacity:** 3.76× more tokens per GiB than bf16 (272 vs 1024 bytes per token).
- **Correctness:** attention over the packed cache is bit-identical to attention over the same dequantized values stored as bf16.
- **No change for other KV dtypes.** The only shared-kernel change is a branch on the cache pointer's element type, which Triton resolves at compile time, so the bf16 and FP8 specializations compile to the same code as before.
- **No speed claim.** The Triton read path unpacks to bf16 before both dots, so it doesn't make attention faster: at 16k tokens it takes about 1.13× as long as bf16 per layer. The gain is capacity. Faster arithmetic over this cache comes in a follow-up.

## Purpose

## Purpose

Fixes #60561.

Since #53781, a device-resident BLHNC MLA cache registers one NIXL region per layer, because
`page_contiguous` is true for every layer. For GLM-5.3 that is 99 descriptors per block instead of
one, so BLHNC transfers cost more than LBHNC's (104 vs 62 strides on a decode rank).

This PR adds `kv_connector_extra_config.whole_row_regions` (default `false`):
- **Replicated (MLA) layers** of a block-major row register as one whole-row region, as they did
  before #53781.
- **Head-sharded layers** (a GQA draft under an MLA target) never take the whole-row branch. They

  - `kv_buffer_device=cpu`;

items.title: [Bugfix] Warm GLM DeepGEMM mHC pre-norm specializations
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash can finish startup and still pause to compile an mHC kernel when a new prompt length arrives. This PR moves those missing compilations to startup without changing the kernel math or split-K heuristic.

Addresses #60536. Depends on https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/29 for the compile-only entry point used by this implementation.

## Claims

- Register every reachable DeepGEMM mHC pre-norm specialization for GLM's configured token range, deduplicated by `(N, K, num_splits)`.
- Compile them through the existing startup warmup registry, without allocating input tensors or launching dummy kernels.
- Keep runtime split selection, kernel math, and backend selection unchanged.

## Details

### Why startup misses these kernels

The mHC pre-norm path contains a matrix multiplication implemented by DeepGEMM. It selects a split-K count (how many pieces to divide the reduction into) based on the number of tokens in the current engine step. Each distinct split count requires a separately compiled kernel. The row count `M` itself is dynamic, so there is no need to compile once per prompt length.

The existing selection is:

```python
num_splits = max(1, min(num_sms // ceil(M / 64), ceil(K / 64) // 4))
```

Here `M` is the step's token count, `K` is the input width, and `N` is the output width. For example, with 78 SMs and `K=16384`, `M=64`, `192`, and `16384` select 64, 26, and 1 splits respectively. Compiling the first and last does not compile the middle one. The number of required specializations depends on the GPU and configured token range; the issue's count of missing variants is not a universal constant.

The startup profile run and CUDA-graph capture exercise only some split counts. GLM does not register the remaining DeepGEMM variants for explicit warmup. items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #60109. This is an alternative to #60117 and #60123.

HiSparse stored GPU residency by editing core block-table rows after sending them: it adopted GPU copies of host prefix pages, and nulled pages the pool reused. The edits reached the worker through `SchedulerOutput.block_table_updates`, and #60109 was a new request's row arriving twice in one step. With this PR, HiSparse owns residency, and core rows stay append-only:

- **Scheduler:** `HiSparseResidentManager` keeps adopted and lost pages as per-request overrides. The coordinator sends the changes in HiSparse's connector metadata.
- **Worker:** HiSparse keeps one persistent device table `[request state rows, resident groups, pages]`, updated with one scatter when residency changes. The decode resolver kernel indexes it by state row, so nothing is copied per step; prefill staging gathers its rows.
- **Core:** `block_table_updates` is removed and `update_requests` is back to its pre-HiSparse form. `add_requests` is unchanged.

**Why this over #60117/#60123:** those keep HiSparse's row edits in core (in `update_requests`, and in `add_requests` for #60123). This removes them entirely. Cost: about 260 lines versus about 10, plus one int32 table: about 18 MB at 256 seqs × 18k context × 61 groups, and about 0.25 GB at 512 seqs × 128k. Native vLLM models name their modules after the checkpoint, so LoRA weights on renamed modules match nothing and get dropped without a warning. This PR catches those adapter keys at load time and maps them back through the reversed renames, using the mappings Transformers already ships.

This is the generalised version of #60131, which hard-codes the rename for GLM-5.3-Flash only. The idea comes from @hmellor, who pointed at how the Transformers modeling backend reuses `WeightRenaming` ([base.py#L318-L320](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4ed4c4433b87e45d72f401f27f1b56c932c90071/vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py#L318-L320)). items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Apply the weight renamings Transformers uses for each checkpoint (`transformers.conversion_mapping`) during weight loading, and update models so they no longer hand-map legacy checkpoint names.   - vLLM's own config classes are converted to the native Transformers config class first. If the model still can't be built, the unscoped renamings of the `model_type` are used.

Part of #60420. When a HiSparse prefill stages history that has spilled to host, two temporaries grow with prompt length:

items.title: [HiSparse] Write mixed decode/prefill attention outputs in place
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Part of #60420. With HiSparse, a mixed batch runs its decode rows and prefill rows as two sparse-MLA kernels and joins them with `torch.cat`. items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Re-plan DSA indexer decode schedule for DBO's reduced DeepGEMM SM count
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

With `--enable-dbo` and an all2all backend that reserves communication SMs (e.g. DeepEP high-throughput), DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x) crash in the sparse-attention indexer as soon as a microbatched step contains a decode-branch request:

```
RuntimeError: Assertion error (csrc/apis/attention.hpp:346): _schedule_meta_size == num_sms + 1 and _meta_info_size == 2
```

The indexer builder plans DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits schedule for the whole GPU, but DBO lowers DeepGEMM's SM count (`set_num_sms(total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS)`) while the microbatches run. This PR re-plans the schedule at the call site when the two counts differ. No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `schedule_meta_size`, `dbo indexer num_sms`, `paged_mqa_logits set_num_sms`: 0 results). Rechecked 2026-10-08 against open PRs: #56476 (DeepSeek-V4.1 per-microbatch index state) also edits `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, in different lines, and does not touch the schedule metadata.

## Claims

- Fixes the DSA indexer decode crash under DBO (Model Runner V1 and V2, CUDA + DeepGEMM).
- The re-planned schedule gives bit-identical indexer logits, so the fix does not change results: with it, GLM-5.3 accuracy under DBO matches DBO with SM partitioning disabled (`VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0`), where this code path never runs.
- Separately, GLM-5.3 accuracy with DBO on is well below DBO off (GSM8K ~0.6 vs 0.93) with or without this change. That is a separate, pre-existing DBO bug in GLM-5.x's shared top-k layers that this crash was hiding, fixed in #60734 (see Validation).
- No cost when the SM count is unchanged (one host-side `get_num_sms()` per indexer layer). Under DBO, one ~9 µs metadata kernel per microbatch per forward, reused by all indexer layers. No host syncs; CUDA-graph safe.
- XPU / ROCm paths unchanged.

## Validation

This branch is rebased onto main @ 240785b8; the rebase did not change the patch (same `git patch-id`). The unit and related tests below were re-run on the rebased commit

items.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Clamp BLOCK_SIZE_K to the FP8 quantization block in the batched Triton MoE
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

`invoke_moe_batched_triton_kernel` (the `BATCHED_TRITON` FP8 MoE used with DeepEP low-latency and other batched-activation all2all backends when DeepGEMM is unavailable or disabled) takes `BLOCK_SIZE_K` straight from the tuned config. With block-quantized FP8 weights the kernel loads one weight and activation scale per `BLOCK_K` tile (`offs_ks = k * BLOCK_K // group_k`), so a `BLOCK_SIZE_K` wider than the 128-wide quantization block applies one block's scale to the next block's values. 53 of the 64 shipped `fp8_w8a8, block_shape=[128,128]` configs pick `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 256 for some batch sizes. The standard path already clamps (`fused_moe.py:843-844`); this PR applies the same clamp in the batched launcher.

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `fused_batched_moe BLOCK_SIZE_K`, `BLOCK_SIZE_K batched fp8`, `batched triton block_shape BLOCK_K`). Rechecked 2026-10-08: open PR #51605 resizes batched Triton MoE tiles on XPU and edits the same launcher, but it does not clamp `BLOCK_SIZE_K` for block-quantized FP8 on CUDA; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Claims

- Fixes wrong outputs from the batched Triton FP8 block-quant MoE whenever the selected config has `BLOCK_SIZE_K` > the quantization block. GLM-5.3 FP8 with DeepEP low-latency and DeepGEMM off: GSM8K 0.02 → 0.93.
- No change when the config already has `BLOCK_SIZE_K` <= 128, for per-token / per-tensor FP8, or for unquantized dtypes (`block_shape is None`).

items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep DSA shared-indexer top-k state per DBO microbatch
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

With `--enable-dbo`, GLM-5.x (DSA with shared top-k layers, `index_topk_freq > 1`) loses about a third of its GSM8K accuracy: 0.93 with DBO off, 0.61 with DBO on. The layers that reuse an earlier layer's sparse-attention top-k (57 of GLM-5.3's 78 layers) read it from buffers that have no microbatch dimension. DBO runs microbatch 1's index-producing layer between microbatch 0's producer and its consumers, so microbatch 0's consumers attend over microbatch 1's token selection. This PR gives every DBO microbatch after the first its own copy of that state. With it, DBO-on accuracy matches DBO off.

Companion to #60732 (DSA indexer crash under DBO, which hid this bug). The two fixes are independent; DBO with DeepEP high-throughput needs both. No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `dbo topk`, `index_topk_freq dbo`, `shared indexer microbatch`, `GLM-5 dbo accuracy`: 0 results). Related open PR: #56476 fixes the same class of bug for DeepSeek-V4.1 (its top-k and candidate buffers, via a new `dbo_select_buffer` helper). It does not cover the DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.x IndexCache path changed here; if it lands first, this PR can switch to its helper.

## Claims

- Fixes GLM-5.x accuracy under DBO on Model Runner V1 and V2: GSM8K 0.61 → 0.92 (DBO off: 0.92–0.93). Also with DBO microbatches replayed from FULL decode CUDA graphs (DeepEP low-latency): 0.44 → 0.85 (DBO off: 0.84–0.86).
- No change without DBO, and none for DSA models without shared top-k layers (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.1: every layer computes its own top-k, so no microbatch state is allocated). Measured: both score the same with DBO on as off, with and without this change, and report identical KV cache memory with and without it.
- Memory under DBO, per GPU and per extra microbatch: `(max_num_batched_tokens + G * (max_decode_rows + 1)) * index_topk * 4` bytes, where `G` is the number of index groups with followers (19 for GLM-5.3). GLM-5.3 at `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=1024`: 216

items.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Keep DeepEP high-throughput buffers alive across DBO streams
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Under DBO, `DeepEPHTPrepareAndFinalize` has DeepEP allocate its dispatch outputs on the DBO comm stream, then reads them on the compute stream; the combine input crosses the other way. The caching allocator is never told about these cross-stream reads, so the other microbatch's next DeepEP call can reuse a block and overwrite it before it is read. With the DeepGEMM FP8 MoE this crashes the engine at startup with an illegal memory access in `ep_scatter`. This PR calls `record_stream` on every tensor that crosses between the two streams.

A GitHub search found no existing issue or PR for this. Related: #46990 added a ROCm-only host sync after HT dispatch/combine under DBO, possibly for the same hazard (see Details). #27666 and #38451 fixed other DBO + DeepEP HT problems.

## Claims

- Fixes the startup crash with DBO + DeepEP high-throughput + the DeepGEMM FP8 MoE (`VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1`, the defaults). For GLM-5.3 FP8 on main, 2 of 2 runs crashed in the first microbatched step without the fix. On 0.29.0, so did all 7 runs that had neither the fix nor a serializing workaround (`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING`, no caching allocator, host sync). With the fix, full GSM8K scores 0.927 with CUTLASS linears and 0.912 with DeepGEMM linears (DBO off: 0.923).
- Covers both directions for every experts backend behind DeepEP HT: DeepEP's outputs (comm stream to compute stream) and the reduced expert output passed to combine (compute stream to comm stream; defensive on main, see Details). With `--enable-dbo`, main runs Model Runner V1 unless `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` is set. MRV2's opt-in DBO uses the same microbatch contexts and streams, so it gets the same fix. Only Model Runner V1 was run.
- No change when DBO is off. With DBO on, there are no host syncs and no extra kernels. The cost is at most 9 `record_stream` calls per MoE layer per microbatch, plus one CUDA event per recorded block when it is freed; the allocator reuses that block only aft

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] MoRIIO: support kernel-block-split 4-D K…
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

On a GLM-5.3-Flash 1P/1D MoRIIO READ deployment, registering the sparse-indexer ("kpool") KV cache aborts with `Unsupported MoRIIO MLA cache shape for layer …self_attn.indexer`. For an `MLAAttentionSpec` carrying a `storage_block_size`, `create_kv_cache_views` hands connectors a **kernel-block-split** 4-D view whose leading dim counts kernel blocks, not manager blocks (`r = block_size / storage_block_size`; `r = 17` at EP8/TP1). MoRIIO's standardized 4-D branch only accepted `r == 1`, so it rejected the indexer view. Block ids on the wire are always manager ids, so geometry must be expressed in manager blocks.

**This PR teaches `get_layer_transfer_geometry` (`moriio_layout.py`) to read kernel-split views in manager blocks:**
- Accept `spec.num_states % N == 0`, derive `r = num_states // N`, and report `num_blocks = B/r`, `block_stride = stride[0]*r`, `block_len = num_states*slot_size`.
- Reject any view that isn't `r` dense, contiguous kernel pages per block, so a malformed layout errors instead of silently transferring wrong bytes.

Bit-identical for `r == 1` (e.g. DeepSeek MLA); no wire-format or metadata change. ~20 lines in one file. (This supersedes the fork's kernel-unit approach — deriving `r` from the view and spec removes the `kbpb`/`layer_num_blocks` protocol additions, since `r` is a per-layer property identical on both legs.)

## Validation

- Unit: `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_kv_layout.py` on MI300X (`vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`, against `origin/main`) — **59 passed**. Added tests cover ratio/head equivalence, a real-allocator GLM kpool-indexer case through `create_kv_cache_views`, and the two rejection paths. Removing the fix reproduces `Unsupported MoRIIO MLA cache shape`.
- `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` and `mypy` pass.
- E2E: this change is required (with the deps below) to boot GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8 1P/1D over MoRIIO READ. On the combined stack both legs boot and disaggregated NIAH recall is correct at 2K/
